item.subject: maths
item.stem:
The diagram shows Yash's triangular dot pattern with rows of 1, then 2, then 3 dots, and a square 3-by-3 dot array.

Which claim connects the triangular pattern to the square pattern?

options.A: Two adjacent triangular totals join into a square: $3+6=9$, matching the 3-by-3 array.
options.B: The whole display is only a square-number pattern, so the triangular rows need no role.
options.C: The square 3-by-3 array is what creates the triangular rows of 1, 2, and 3 dots.
options.D: The answer is 9 only because 9 is the largest count printed beside the arrays.
